full_name: W. Ralph Eubanks | Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University
title: 2021–2022 Journalism & Nonfiction Carl and Lily Pforzheimer Foundation Fellow University of Mississippi
bio: W. Ralph Eubanks is a writer and essayist whose work focuses on race, identity, and the culture and literature of the American South. His most recent book, A Place Like Mississippi: A Journey Through A Real and Imagined Literary Landscape (Timber Press, 2021), examines how a small state that rests by the banks of a great river has made so many contributions to American letters, carrying an outsized role in the national imagination. He is also the author of two other works of nonfiction, Ever Is a Long Time: A Journey into Mississippi’s Dark Past (Basic Books, 2003) and The House at the End of the Road: The Story of Three Generations of an Interracial Family in the American South (Smithsonian, 2009). He is a visiting professor of English and Southern studies at the University of Mississippi.
